messages.subject: Estimating P, getP vs linearComb
parts:
Hello,
I am fairly new to the unmarked and was hoping to get some clarification about the outputs from getP vs linearComb methods. 

We conducted three traditional surveys for turtles, as well as collected three individual water samples for eDNA analysis during one of the three traditional surveys. We have decided that our collection method/data does not meet the requirements for a three level occupancy model (Schmidt et al 2013). One of our objectives is to therefore make ad hoc comparisons of the two survey methods. We fitted two separate occupancy models (traditional and eDNA) and have generated occupancy and detection estimates for both.

My question is in regards to generating detection estimates for the basic, two-level occupancy model (MacKenzie 2002). I understand that this may be more dependent on a researcher's specific objectives, but I was wondering which method (linearComb or getP) was more preferred for generating detection estimates. If I understand the two methods correctly, put very simply, the linearComb method returns p under specific covariate conditions (I set my covariates to their means), while getP returns expected detection probabilities based on the actual data (i.e. the detection conditions during the survey). 

If I wanted to generate a summary table of my candidate models and their associated occupancy and detection estimates, which method (getP or linearComb) should be used? In my case, the two methods have very different outputs.


Example code:
backTransform(linearComb(mod9, coefficients = c(1, 0, 0), type = 'det')) #detection covariates set to their means

or

getP(mod9) #take average of this output



Thank you very much for any assistance with this matter!
Ellery

(I can provide additional code and data if needed!)
